newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - July 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - July 9.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- A new law endorsed by the Executive Council, the inner cabinet of Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa, was due to be passed by the Provisional Legislature on Wednesday that would send back children to China who have the right of abode in Hong Kong but who entered the territory illegally.

-- Liao Hui, now in charge of Beijing's affairs concerning overseas Chinese and relations with Taiwan, will replace Lu Ping as the director of the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office. Liao's family has strong connections in Taiwan and his appointment will help influence the island to adopt the "one country, two systems" concept that set out Hong Kong's handover to the mainland.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL - The People's Bank of China set up a limited company in Hong Kong last month which acts as a trader and investment consultant. Since the company was allowed to provide investment suggestions to Beijing and get involved in Hong Kong's financial market, it is likely the firm would help handle China's foreign reserves.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Democratic Party member and former legislator Lee Chuk-yan started a 120-hour hunger strike to protest against the new government's decision to suspend seven bills on human rights and labour rights which were rushed through by the old Legislative Council before the handover.

-- Research by an Australian institute shows China ranks the lowest among 11 Asia-Pacific countries in terms of the degree of freedom allowed in the country. Australia had the highest degree of freedom in the region, the study said.
-- WEN WEI PO -- China prosecuted more than 5,000 cadres for corruption in the first five months of the year and the government has called for thorough investigations.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- A U.S. Senate hearing heard that top Chinese officials were directly involved in channelling illegal political donations to presidential candidates and congressmen during the 1996 campaign.

-- Former Merrill Lynch private banker Kevin Wallace was arrested with another man amid allegations by his former employer that he engaged in unauthorised trading, falsifying client statements and forgery.

-- HONG KONG STANDARD -- Despite pressure from the shipping industry and cargo handlers on both sides of the Taiwan Straits, Beijing had postponed plans to open more mainland ports to direct shipping from Taiwan for fear that could weaken Hong Kong's status as an international transshipment centre.
